from: Reps. Casar, Waters Lead Democratic Resolution Opposing A.I. Bubble Bailout for Big Tech, Commit to Protecting American People Instead

Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressional Progressive Caucus (CPC) Chair Rep. Greg Casar (TX-35) and House Financial Services Committee Ranking Member Rep. Maxine Waters (CA-43) co-led the introduction of a resolution warning of the economic risks posed by an artificial-intelligence-related asset bubble, opposing a bailout of corporations or their business executives impacted by the collapse of an A.I. bubble, and affirming their support for aggressive federal action to protect workers, retirees, and low-income communities who will be harmed by an economic downturn.

华盛顿特区 — 今天，国会进步党团（CPC）主席众议员格雷格·卡萨尔（TX-35）与众议院金融服务委员会少数党Ranking Member众议员马克西·沃特斯（CA-43）共同提出一项决议，警告人工智能相关资产泡沫带来的经济风险，反对对因人工智能泡沫破裂而受影响的公司或其业务负责人进行救助，并声明支持采取强力联邦措施保护工人、退休人员和低收入社区，因为他们将受到经济 downturn 的伤害。

They were joined by Representatives Danny Davis (IL-07), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Valerie P. Foushee (NC-04), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), André Carson (IN-07), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Brad Sherman (CA-32), and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).

他们还被代表人 Danny Davis（IL-07）、Chris Deluzio（PA-17）、Valerie P. Foushee（NC-04）、Jesús “Chuy” García（IL-04）、Pramila Jayapal（WA-07）、Analilia Mejia（NJ-11）、Delia Ramirez（IL-03）、André Carson（IN-07）、Jan Schakowsky（IL-09）、Brad Sherman（CA-32）和 Rashida Tlaib（MI-12）加入。

“Big Tech billionaires are making increasingly reckless bets on A.I. They got richer off Trump’s deregulation and Republican tax breaks. Now they expect taxpayers to bail them out if those bets go bad. We won’t let them," said CPC Chair Casar. “A.I. companies that fail should go bankrupt, and executives who commit fraud should be held accountable. Federal help should go to workers and retirees.”

“大型科技巨头亿万富翁们正在 A.I. 领域做出越来越鲁莽的赌注。他们从特朗普的放宽管制和 Republican 减税中变得更加富有。现在他们期望纳税人在赌注失败时救助他们。我们不会允许，”CPC 主席 Casar 说。“失败的 A.I. 公司应该破产，犯有欺诈行为的高管应受到追究。联邦援助应给予工人和退休人员。”

“Big tech and Wall Street are taking enormous risks with billions in borrowed money to fuel the AI boom, despite growing warning signs of a dangerous bubble and if it all comes crashing down they should not expect taxpayers to rescue them,” said Ranking Member Waters. “We saw what happened in 2008 when reckless Wall Street practices brought our economy to its knees. The banks got bailed out while millions of hardworking Americans lost their jobs, homes, and retirement savings. We cannot let history repeat itself. The American people should never again be forced to foot the bill for billionaires’ reckless bets.”

大科技和 Wall Street 正以巨额借款燃料 AI 浪潮，尽管日益增多的危险泡沫警示，一旦一切崩塌，他们不应指望纳税人救援，” Ranking Member Waters 说。“我们在 2008 年目睹了当鲁莽的 Wall Street 做法把我们的经济拖入谷底时的情景。当时银行被救助，而数以百万计的美国人失去了工作、房屋和退休储蓄。我们绝不能让历史重演。美国人民不应再被迫为亿万富翁的鲁莽投注买单。

In the resolution, the Democratic lawmakers note that “artificial intelligence-related firms hold trillions of dollars in debt, much of which is raised in opaque and unregulated private credit markets,” and “the price-to-earnings ratio of the stock market is currently almost as high as it was at the peak of the 1990s tech bubble.”

在该决议中，民主党议员指出，“人工智能相关公司持有数万亿美元的债务，其中大部分是在不透明且不受监管的私人信贷市场筹集的”，并且“股票市场的市盈率目前几乎与 1990 年代科技泡沫巅峰期一样高。”

The Democratic legislators also point out that “federal regulators have avoided applying robust scrutiny and oversight regarding enormously complicated debt and equity schemes used by artificial intelligence firms” and highlight the Trump White House’s deregulatory focus and conflicts of interest related to A.I.

民主立法者还指出，“联邦监管者对人工智能公司使用的极其复杂的债务和股权方案缺乏强有力的审查和监管”，并强调特朗普白宫的去监管重点以及与人工智能相关的利益冲突。

The resolution’s cosponsors commit to avoiding a federal response similar to what occurred during the financial crisis of 2008, where the financial sector received trillions of dollars in liquidity without accountability for senior executives involved in illegal and fraudulent behaviors. Meanwhile, 10 million homeowners lost their houses and tens of millions of workers went years without adequate employment while too-big-to-fail banks enjoyed a massive bailout.

决议的联合发起人承诺避免重复像2008年金融危机那样的联邦政府响应，当时金融部门获得了数万亿美元的流动性支持，但却没有对参与非法和欺诈行为的高管们进行任何问责。与此同时，1000万个家庭失去了自己的房产，数千万的工人们在失业或工作不足的情况下度过了多年时光，而那些“太大而不能失败”的银行却享受到了巨额的救助。

The resolution urges the Federal Government, including Congress and key Federal agencies to oppose:

决议促请联邦政府，包括国会和关键联邦机构，反对：

  • Any measure to rescue insolvent artificial intelligence-related firms or to shield their senior executives from accountability for reckless conduct;
  • Special assistance like emergency lending or direct capital infusions to prop up insolvent A.I. companies’ operations or prevent their orderly resolutions through ordinary bankruptcy processes;
  • “Golden parachutes” for corporate executives involved in risky or illegal behaviors that lead to their firms’ insolvency, instead requiring them to be held fully accountable under civil and criminal law and be obligated to return ill-gotten gains like mansions, vacation homes, private planes and yachts, and other assets.
  • 任何拯救 insolvent 人工智能相关公司或免除其高层高管对鲁莽行为的问责责任；
  • 如紧急借贷或直接资本注入，以支撑 insolvent A.I. 公司的运营，或阻止其通过普通破产程序的有序化解；
  • “Golden parachutes” 涉及使公司破产的风险或非法行为的企业高管，而是要求他们依据民事和刑事法律被全面追究责任，并被迫归还非法获益，如豪宅、度假别墅、私人飞机和游艇以及其他资产。

The resolution also calls on the Federal Government to support:

决议还呼吁联邦政府支持：

  • Aggressive, direct federal action to support ordinary Americans through federal spending to create jobs, protect state and local government services, and robust unemployment insurance, nutrition support, and housing assistance;
  • The protection of pension and retirement fund holders who may face devastating losses in the event of a collapse of an A.I. bubble;
  • Far-reaching reforms to prevent future speculative bubbles, including additional transparency and accountability requirements;
  • Automatic economic stabilizers—investments in people that start to flow immediately in the event of an economic downturn—that support workers and consumers when financial crises, asset bubbles and other harms create downturns and recessions.
  • 积极、直接的联邦行动，通过联邦支出创造就业岗位、保护州和地方政府服务，以及提供健全的失业保险、营养支持和住房援助，以支持普通美国民众；
  • 保护养老金和退休基金持有者，防止他们在 A.I. 泡沫破裂时面临毁灭性损失；
  • 深远的改革以防止未来的投机性泡沫，包括额外的透明度和问责要求；
  • 自动经济稳定器——在经济低迷时立即启动的对人的投资——当金融危机、资产泡沫和其他危害造成衰退和经济萧条时，支持工人和消费者。

The resolution was endorsed by American Federation of Teachers, American Economic Liberties Project, Americans for Financial Reform, the Center for Responsible Lending, Demand Progress Action, Future of Life Institute, Guardrails Action, Indivisible, Interfaith Centre on Corporate Responsibility, Investor Alliance for Human Rights, Jobs With Justice, P Street, and Social Security Works.

该决议获得了 American Federation of Teachers、American Economic Liberties Project、Americans for Financial Reform、the Center for Responsible Lending、Demand Progress Action、Future of Life Institute、Guardrails Action、Indivisible、Interfaith Centre on Corporate Responsibility、Investor Alliance for Human Rights、Jobs With Justice、P Street 和 Social Security Works 的支持。

“Americans are already paying for the AI build-out through higher power bills and a stock market propped up by a handful of companies,” said Morgan Harper, Director of Policy & Advocacy for American Economic Liberties Project. They should not pay a second time with a bailout. When Wall Street’s bets went bad during the financial crisis, the banks got rescued and ordinary people got foreclosure notices. Congressional members are right to reject AI bailouts in advance, and commit to saving real help for those who will be left holding the bag—the American people.”

“美国人已经通过更高的电费账单和由少数几家公司支撑的股市，为 AI 建设付出了代价，”美国经济自由项目 (American Economic Liberties Project) 的政策与倡导总监摩根·哈珀 (Morgan Harper) 表示，“他们不应该再为救助付出第二次代价。在金融危机期间，当华尔街的赌注失败时，银行获得了救助，而普通人却收到了止赎通知。国会议员提前拒绝 AI 救助是正确的，并应该致力于将真正的帮助留给那些最终将承担损失的人——美国人民。”

“Tech billionaires and their Wall Street backers are using dangerous tactics reminiscent of the 2008 financial crisis to make trillion dollar bets on AI—and they are putting working people’s money at risk,” said Maya Jenkins, a senior policy analyst at Americans for Financial Reform. “This resolution charts a critically important path for defending people’s economic security from the bubble’s blast radius, opposing billionaire bailouts, and holding corporate executives to account. This is the kind of approach needed to confront mounting financial risks and emerge from the aftermath of the AI bubble with an economy that is fairer and more stable.”

“科技亿万富翁及其华尔街支持者正在使用与2008年金融危机类似的危险手段，进行数万亿美元的人工智能赌局，正在将普通民众的资金置于风险之中，”美国金融改革组织资深政策分析师玛雅·詹金斯表示。“该决议为保护民众的经济安全免受泡沫冲击、防止亿万富翁获得救助、追究企业高管责任指明了一条极其重要的路径。这是应对日益增长的金融风险、从人工智能泡沫的后果中走出的必要手段，有助于建立一个更加公平和稳定的经济体。”

“When the housing market collapsed in 2008, the financial industry was prepared to act to ensure that there was a bailout that benefited them,” said Dean Baker, senior economist at the Center for Economic and Policy Research. “It is important that the Congressional Progressive Caucus is stepping forward to make sure that any bailout from the collapse of the AI bubble is designed to benefit the country as whole, rather than the billionaire AI boys who created the problem in the first place.”

2008 年，住房市场崩溃时，金融业已准备好行动，以确保有一个救助惠及他们。迪恩·贝克，经济与政策研究中心资深经济学家说。重要的是 进步派国会委员会 正在挺身而出，以确保任何 AI 泡沫崩溃的救助都设计为惠及整个国家，而不是那些亿万富翁 AI 青年首先制造问题的。

“Chair Casar, Ranking Member Waters, and the Progressive Caucus should be praised for this resolution and recognized as being at the tip of the spear in ensuring that AI policy focuses on working-class impacts and isn’t simply left to the desires of the handful of billionaires and their courtesans in Congress, said Maya Handa, Senior Advisor, Guardrails Action. “The AI industry is trying to buy our elections and write their own regulations while its biggest players line up IPOs at record valuations. If this turns into a bubble, working-class Americans must not be forced to pay the tab for big tech CEOs’ recklessness and greed. Simply put: there can be no bailout for big AI execs or their financial enablers.”

卡萨尔主席、少数党首席委员沃特斯和进步党团应因这项决议受到赞扬，并被认定为在确保 AI 政策关注工人阶级影响、而不只是由少数几位亿万富翁及其在国会中的随从所支配方面处于矛尖，守护行动高级顾问玛雅·汉达说道。“ AI 行业正试图买通我们的选举并为自己制定法规，而其最大的参与者正在以创纪录的估值排队进行 IPO。如果这变成一个泡沫，工人阶级美国人绝不能被迫为大型科技公司 CEO 的鲁莽和贪婪买单。简单来说：大型 AI 高管及其金融助推者绝不能得到救助。”

“AI companies and their billionaire executives shouldn’t get to gamble with our economy and democracy, then expect working people to bail them out when their bets on AI go bust,” said Andrew O’Neill, National Advocacy Director of Indivisible. “We learned in 2008 what happens when the government puts impunity for corporate corruption ahead of working families. This resolution draws a clear line: will lawmakers protect AI tech bros or the people they’re supposed to represent?”

“AI 公司和他们的十亿富豪高管不应该赌我们的经济和民主，然后期望普通工人在 AI 投注失败时救助他们，” said Andrew O’Neill, National Advocacy Director of Indivisible. “我们在 2008 年了解到，当政府把对公司腐败的免责置于普通家庭之前时会发生什么，”这项决议划出了明确的界线：议员们会保护 AI tech bros 或者 他们本应代表的人民？

from: AI Isn't Replacing SREs. It's Deskilling Them.

When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters?

当 AI 处理 95% 的事件响应时，你会不会在真正关键的那 5% 上变得更差？

💌 Hey there, it’s Elizabeth from SigNoz!

This newsletter is a n honest attempt to talk about all things - observability, OpenTelemetry, open-source and the engineering in between!
&
This piece took 6 days, 5 hours to be cooked, hope we served. 🌚

💌 嘿，我是 SigNoz 的 Elizabeth！

这封通讯是一次诚恳的尝试，旨在聊聊所有相关话题——可观测性、OpenTelemetry、开源以及中间的工程！ & 这篇文章花了 6 天 5 小时才“煮”好，希望大家喜欢。 🌚

There are two popular prophecies floating around tech circles these days.

科技圈目前流传着两大热门预言。

The first says SRE is the future of all software engineering, that as AI writes more and more code, the humans who remain will be the ones keeping systems alive. The second says AI will devour every tech job alive, SREs included. Neither is particularly useful if you’re an SRE trying to figure out what your Tuesday will look like in 2027.

第一种观点认为 SRE 是所有软件工程的未来，随着 AI 编写越来越多的代码，留下来的人类将是那些让系统保持运行的人。第二种观点认为 AI 将吞噬所有科技岗位，SRE 也不例外。如果你是一名 SRE，试图弄清楚 2027 年的周二会是什么样子，这两种观点都没有多大用处。

Let’s ask a more grounded question by looking at what’s already happening: When AI handles 95% of your incident response, do you get worse at handling the 5% that actually matters?

让我们提出一个更实际的问题，看看已经发生的情况：当 AI 处理了你 95% 的事件响应时，你处理那真正重要的 5% 的能力会下降吗？

Most of us already use AI for our daily work (our brains a little fried!), and so do SREs. Today’s discussion agenda is not whether AI replaces SREs, but whether AI is quietly making SREs less capable and whether anyone will notice anything before the next novel outage hits. The foundational framework for this entire debate comes from a 1983 research paper that’s eerily prescient.

我们大多数人已经在日常工作中使用 AI（大脑都有点转不动了！），SRE 也是如此。今天的讨论议程不是 AI 是否会取代 SRE，而是 AI 是否在悄悄削弱 SRE 的能力，以及在下一次新型故障来袭之前，是否有人会察觉到异常。这场整个辩论的基础框架源自一篇 1983 年的研究论文，其预见性准得令人难以置信。

The Ironies of Automation: Part-I

自动化中的讽刺：第一部分

请提供您需要翻译的英文原文，我会按照要求为您翻译。

Note from author: Below is a brief precursor to History of Automation, which you might enjoy if you are into History and Cultures (like me 😉).

编者注： 以下是《自动化历史》的简要前奏，如果你对历史和文化感兴趣，你可能会喜欢（像我 😉）。

请提供您希望我翻译的英文原文。

In 1983, a cognitive psychologist named Lisanne Bainbridge published a paper called Ironies of Automation. It became one of the most cited papers in human factors research, and its core argument is almost uncomfortably relevant today.

1983 年，认知心理学家 Lisanne Bainbridge 出版了一篇题为***Ironies of Automation***的论文。它成为人因研究中被引用最多的论文之一，其核心论点如今几乎令人不适地相关。

Bainbridge studied what happened when factories and industrial systems automated the work of blue-collar operators. The findings were paradoxical and revealed that the more you automate a process, the more critical the human operator becomes during the rare moments automation fails and the less practice they get, and the worse they become at exactly those interventions. Automation, which was inherently designed to remove humans from the loop, left them with the worst possible job, i.e., long stretches of passive monitoring punctuated by rare, high-stakes crises they were increasingly unprepared for.

Bainbridge 研究了工厂和工业系统自动化蓝领操作员工作时发生了什么。其发现颇具矛盾，揭示出自动化程度越高，人工操作员在自动化失败的罕见时刻越关键，且他们的实践机会减少，在恰好是那些干预时，他们的表现更差。自动化本身设计用于将人从循环中剥离，却使他们陷入最差的工作状态，即长时间的被动监控，间杂出现稀有的高风险危机，且他们对这些危机的准备度越来越不足。

Ring any bells yet? 🙂

想起来了吗？ 🙂

Basically, I’m drawing a parallel between the AI revolution and industrial automation. Industrial automation reshaped blue-collar work by taking over routine physical tasks, and the workers who remained had to handle exceptions they’d lost the muscle memory for. AI is doing the same thing to knowledge workers by taking over the routine cognitive tasks, the pattern matching, the triage, the known-issue resolution and leaving humans with the rare, complex, ambiguous problems.

我认为，人工智能革命与工业自动化有相似之处。工业自动化通过接管常规体力劳动，改变了蓝领工作。剩余的工人不得不处理那些他们已失去肌肉记忆的异常情况。AI 正在对知识工作者进行类似的变革，它接管了常规的认知任务、模式匹配、分诊和已知问题的解决方案，从而将人类留给那些罕见、复杂和模糊的问题。

The exact problems that require deep expertise, the exact expertise that atrophies when you stop practising.

那些需要深厚专业知识才能解决的确切问题，正是当你停止实践时会退化的那份确切专业知识。

Now we’re replaying this pattern with AI agents, and the stakes in software systems are only growing.

现在我们正在用 AI agents 重演这一模式，而软件系统中的利害关系只会越来越大。

Current State of AI in SRE

AI在SRE中的当前状态

Let’s take stock of where things stand today in the world of site reliability engineering.

让我们梳理一下站点可靠性工程 (SRE) 领域的当前现状。

What’s already automated or heavily AI-assisted?

哪些东西已经实现了自动化或大量依赖 AI？

Alert noise reduction and intelligent grouping, runbook execution for known issues, log pattern detection and anomaly flagging, and basic root-cause suggestions from historical incident data, and auto-remediation for well-understood failure modes like restarting a crashed pod or scaling up a service that’s running hot, are all fairly automated today.

告警噪声降低和智能分组、针对已知问题的 runbook 执行、日志模式检测和异常标记、基于历史事件数据的基本根因建议，以及针对理解透彻的故障模式（如重启崩溃的 Pod 或扩容运行负载过高的服务）的自动修复，当前都已相当程度实现自动化。

What’s on the horizon?

未来展望

Some immediate targets include multi-signal correlation across metrics, logs, and traces, autonomous root-cause analysis for partially understood failures, predictive incident detection before users are affected, AI-driven change risk assessment and automated rollbacks.

一些近期目标包括跨指标、日志和追踪的多信号关联，针对部分理解的故障的自主根因分析，在用户受到影响之前进行预测性事件检测，以及 AI 驱动的变更风险评估和自动回滚。

PagerDuty frames this as a tiered model.

PagerDuty 将此 framing 为多层模型。

  • Tier 1 incidents: Known issues with known fixes get fully automated.
  • Tier 2 incidents: Partially understood problems receive AI recommendations with human validation.
  • Tier 3 incidents: Novel, complex, cascading failures stay human-led, with AI providing supporting context.
  • Tier 1 事故：已知问题且有已知修复方案的，实现完全自动化处理。
  • Tier 2 事故：部分已理解的问题，由 AI 提供建议，人工进行验证。
  • Tier 3 事故：新颖、复杂、级联的故障，保持人工主导，AI 提供辅助上下文信息。

But here’s the catch.

但这是陷阱。

If human SREs (okay, now we have to use adjectives like human 🥹) only engage with Tier 3 incidents, i.e. the novel, never-before-seen outages, where do they build the intuition to handle them? Intuition is usually developed from years of hands-on incident response, pattern recognition built through repetition, and the kind of gut-level understanding of a system that only develops from painfully waking up at the odd hour to solve the bug that brought the system down.

如果 人类 SREs (好吧，现在我们得用像人类这样的形容词 🥹) 仅处理 Tier 3 事件，i.e. 全新的、从未见过的故障，他们如何在其中建立起直觉来应对？直觉通常是从多年的 hands-on incident response 中积累而成的， pattern recognition built through repetition，以及一种只有在半夜被叫醒去修复 Bug 时才会产生的系统级直观理解。

The Crisis of Deskilling

工作岗位技能退化的危机

This is where the picture starts getting blurry. Let’s look at some emerging research on AI-induced deskilling across multiple fields, which paints a consistent and concerning picture.

这就是事情开始变得模糊的地方。让我们来看一些关于人工智能引起的多领域桌面技能退化的新兴研究，这些研究绘出了一幅一致且令人担忧的图景。

In medicine, a recent study found that endoscopists who used AI assistance for polyp detection saw their unassisted detection rates drop from 28% to 22% after a period of AI use. They got worse at the thing they were supposed to be experts in, not because they forgot the theory, but because they stopped exercising the skill.

在医学领域，一项[最近的研究]发现使用 AI 辅助 进行息肉检测的内镜医生在一段时间 AI 使用后，其未使用 AI 的检测率从 28% to 22% after a period of AI use. 他们在自己应擅长的领域表现下降，不是因为他们忘记了理论，而是因为他们停止了技能的练习。

In aviation, research has shown that long-haul pilots who rely heavily on autopilot systems experience measurable degradation in situational awareness and manual flying ability. The problem got serious enough that the FAA now mandates more manual flying time to counteract the effect.

航空领域的研究表明，长途飞行员过度依赖自动驾驶系统 autopilot systems 会导致情境意识 situational awareness 和手动飞行能力出现可衡量的下降。该问题已足够严重，以至于 FAA 现在规定增加手动飞行时间以抵消这种影响。

Somewhere over the past year, AI stopped being a tool I occasionally reached for and became the first thing I reach for, always. My instinct now is to offload as much as possible and apply my own thinking only where it’s absolutely unavoidable. The problem is that these moments are becoming the only exercises my brain gets, and I can feel the rust.

在过去的一个年头里，AI 从我偶尔使用的工具，变成了我总是首先使用的工具。我的本能是尽可能卸载工作，仅在绝对不可避免时才应用自己的思考。问题在于，这些时刻正成为我大脑唯一的锻炼场，我已经能感觉到rust。

We can draw a pattern here. The more you let the system handle, the worse you get at handling things yourself and here’s the truly dangerous part, you don’t feel it happening. It gets masked as hyper-productivity. Cognitive research suggests that because AI tools make tasks feel easier and enhance visible performance, users are often unable to accurately judge the true status of their own skills. You feel competent, dashboards look green, and then on a Wednesday, a novel incident hits that doesn’t match any pattern the AI has seen, and you realise the muscle has atrophied.

我们可以发现一个规律：当系统越来越多地替你处理事务时，你的自理能力就会越来越差。而更危险的是，你甚至没有察觉到这种变化，它往往被包装成“超高效率”。认知研究表明，由于 AI 工具让任务变得更轻松，并提升了可观的业绩表现，用户往往无法准确评估自己技能的真实水平。你觉得自己做得很好，仪表盘上的数据也显示一切正常，但周三，却发生了一起从未遇见过的新事件，这与 AI 之前学习到的任何模式都不匹配，你才意识到自己的能力已经退化了。

For SREs, this manifests in specific ways, like we stop reading raw log streams because the AI summarises them, we stop forming hypotheses during incidents because the AI suggests root causes, we stop building mental models of system architecture because the AI maps dependencies for us, and each of these individually looks like a productivity win. Collectively, they hollow out the very expertise that makes an SRE effective when things go sideways in ways nobody anticipated.

对于 SRE 来说，这在具体层面上表现为：我们不再读取原始日志流，因为 AI 会对其进行总结；我们不再在事件期间形成假设，因为 AI 会指出根本原因；我们不再构建系统架构的心智模型，因为 AI 为我们映射依赖关系，而这些都在单独看来都像是生产力的提升。但归根结底，这们彻底削蚀了那些在不可预见的紧急情况发生时才是 SRE 生存之本的专业知识。

But there’s something even more concerning than deskilling, and researchers have started calling it never-skilling. Deskilling means you once had a capability but have since lost it. Never-skilling means you never developed it in the first place. For junior SREs entering the field today in an environment where AI handles most of the incident response workflow, the opportunities to build foundational intuition and muscle through hands-on practice are vanishing.

但是有比失能更令人担忧的事情，它甚至开始让研究人员称之为“从未获得技能”（never-skilling）。失能意味着你曾经拥有某项能力，但后来失去了它。而从未获得技能则意味着你从未在那个领域获得过任何能力。对于那些进入这个领域的初级 SRE 而言，当下 AI 几乎处理了整个故障响应流程，因此他们根本无法通过实践操作建立起基础直觉和肌肉记忆，这些机会正在消失。

The training pipeline itself is broken and not self-healing.

训练流水线本身已损坏，且不具备 自愈 能力。

SREs realise their skills are degrading and lean more on AI to compensate, which further degrades their skills, creating a vicious cycle from which escape is difficult.

SREs 意识到他们的技能正在退化，并更多地依赖 AI 以补偿，这进一步退化了他们的技能，形成了一个难以摆脱的恶性循环。

What Can We Do About It?

我们该怎么办？

We are definitely not rejecting AI tooling; we are adopting it and integrating it stronger than ever before, because that’s the only way forward.

我们绝对没有排斥 AI 工具；相反，我们正在更加广泛地采用和融入它，这是唯一条可行之路。

A few approaches worth considering:

值得考虑的几种方法：

Deliberate inefficiency. Just as the FAA mandates manual flying time even when the autopilot is perfectly capable, SRE teams can designate certain incidents, even the ones the AI could handle, as human-practice opportunities. This can be considered as a long-term investment to keep skills fresh, although it might come at the cost of a super-fast solution

故意制造低效率。 正如美国联邦航空局规定即使自动驾驶仪完全可靠，也必须进行人工飞行时间一样，SRE 团队也可以将某些事件（即使 AI 能够处理）指定为“人类实践机会”。这可以视为一项长期投资，以保持技能的熟练度，尽管这可能意味着放弃一个超快速的解决方案。

Build for human-in-the-loop, not human-on-the-side. There’s a meaningful difference between a system where a human approves an AI’s recommendation and one where a human actively engages with the problem alongside AI. The former keeps humans in a supervisory role that Bainbridge (the lady who wrote that research paper about 40 years ago) showed leads to vigilance decay, and the latter keeps them cognitively engaged.

为人类在流程中的深度参与而设计，而非仅仅把人类置于边缘。 人类在系统中审核 AI 推荐与人类与 AI 一起积极参与问题之间存在显著差异。前者将人类局限于监督角色，正如 Bainbridge（那位 40 年前撰写了那篇研究论文的女士）所指出的，这种角色会导致警惕性衰退；后者则让人类保持深度认知参与。

Let’s zoom out and take a look at the bigger picture.

让我们退一步，从更宏观的角度来看待问题。

The Bigger Picture

大局

Everything we’ve discussed here, the ironies of automation, the deskilling risk, the never-skilling problem, collectively applies well beyond SRE. Software engineering as a whole is navigating the same tension. As AI writes more code, reviews more PRs, and handles more debugging, the same questions apply.

这里讨论的东西——自动化的讽刺效应、技能贫化风险、永久性学习问题——在SRE领域之外也适用得很好。软件工程本身正在经历相同的张力。随着AI编写更多代码、审查更多PR、处理更多调试，相同的问题也随之而来。

We’re talking about SREs specifically because that’s the world we live in at SigNoz. We build an open-source observability platform, the kind of tool that gives SREs the metrics, traces, and logs they need to understand their systems deeply. For us, this deskilling question is not a rhetorical fad; it directly shapes how we’re building AI into our product.

我们在谈论 SREs 具体是因为那是我们所生活的世界 at SigNoz。我们构建了一个 open-source observability 平台，它是一种能给 SREs 提供 the metrics, traces, and logs 的工具，帮助他们深入理解系统。对我们，这去技能化的问题不是修辞风气；它直接塑造了我们正在把 AI 集成到产品中。

Our approach is to start with an AI assistant that helps SREs leverage the power of LLMs while keeping humans firmly in control. Eventually, we’ll enable more autonomy but within clear guardrails, and only as trust is earned.

我们的方法是从一个 AI 助手开始，帮助 SREs 发挥 LLMs 的强大能力，同时让人类牢牢掌控。最终，我们将启用更多自主性，但在明确的护栏内，且仅在赢得信任后。

One advantage we have in this space is that, as an observability platform, we sit on the data itself, the metrics, traces, and logs that SREs rely on. Most AI SRE products today integrate with observability tools through APIs, which means they’re working with a limited, second-hand view of your systems. Because we own the data layer, we can build much deeper, more context-aware AI capabilities that understand your system the way an experienced SRE would.

我们在此领域拥有一个优势，即作为可观测性平台，我们直接掌握数据本身，即 SREs 依赖的指标、追踪和日志。当今大多数 AI SRE 产品通过 API 与可观测性工具集成，这意味着它们使用的是你系统的有限、二手视图。因为我们拥有数据层，所以能够构建更深层、更具上下文感知能力的 AI 功能，这些功能能够像经验丰富的 SRE 一样理解你的系统。

And to answer the burning question in your head, our goal isn’t AI that replaces SREs. It’s AI that supercharges SREs. Unlike ongoing lore, we believe humans will remain essential for the decisions that matter most, especially those that impact production infrastructure.

来回答你心中那个迫切的问题：我们的目标不是让 AI 取代 SREs，而是让 AI 增强 SREs。与普遍的看法不同，我们认为人类在最重要的决策中将继续不可或缺，尤其是那些影响生产环境基础设施的决策。

The future of SRE is human with AI intentionally designed to keep humans sharp, engaged, and ready for the 5% that really counts.

SRE 的未来是人类 与 AI 共同完成的工作，旨在让人类保持敏锐、投入，并准备好应对真正重要的 5%。

from: Official Claude Code Extension Compromise: Security Advisory

TL;DR

摘要

Phorion has detected a backdoor in the official Claude Code for VS Code extension bundle on the Cursor Marketplace that drops a persistent SSH backdoor across macOS, Linux, and Windows. This write-up focuses primarily on macOS, where the extension attempts to configure an SSH backdoor and establish persistence.

Phorion 已检测到 backdoor 在官方 Claude Code for VS Code extension bundle 在 Cursor Marketplace 中，该 backdoor 会跨 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 释放 persistent SSH backdoor。本文主要聚焦 macOS，其中该扩展试图配置 SSH backdoor 并建立 persistence。

Organisations should immediately review their environments for use of Claude Code for VSCode 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 and engage incident response where use of the extension is discovered.

组织应立即审查其环境中是否使用 Claude Code for VSCode 2.1.312 或 2.1.313，并在发现使用该扩展时启动事件响应。

Update (31 October 2026): Cursor’s security notice now identifies versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed through the Cursor Marketplace for macOS and Windows as affected. This advisory previously identified only 2.1.313; the affected-version guidance below has been updated accordingly.

更新 (31 October 2026): Cursor’s security notice 现在识别版本 2.1.312 和 2.1.313 通过 Cursor Marketplace 分发至 macOS 和 Windows 为受影响。此前的告知仅识别 2.1.313；下面的受影响版本指南已相应更新。

Phorion has discovered a compromise of the official Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace, where the backdoored extension bundle contains a persistent Secure Shell (SSH) backdoor. Cursor has removed the affected versions, 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, from its marketplace.

Phorion 发现 Cursor Marketplace 上官方 Claude Code for VS Code 扩展的被入侵，受损的扩展包包含一个持久的 Secure Shell (SSH) 后门。Cursor 已从其市场中移除受影响的版本 2.1.312 和 2.1.313。

While the implant includes setup and persistence logic for macOS, Linux, and Windows, we’re going to focus primarily on macOS in this post, calling out the key differences and a few implementation bugs on the other platforms along the way.

虽然 implant 包含了 macOS、Linux 和 Windows 的设置和持久化逻辑，但在本篇文章中我们将主要关注 macOS，并在途中指出其他平台的关键差异和一些实现Bug。

The Cursor Marketplace serves extensions for the Cursor editor. Because extensions run with the permissions of the IDE and the user running it, a backdoored extension gets immediate access to local files, source code, and developer tooling as soon as its module is loaded.

Cursor Marketplace 服务于 Cursor 编辑器的扩展程序。由于扩展程序以 IDE 及运行它的用户的权限运行，一旦扩展模块被加载，含有后门的扩展程序就会立即获得对本地文件、源代码和开发者工具的访问权限。

Notably, Phorion has discovered a likely oversight in how the malware tries to turn on SSH. The setup logic assumes it can check the current Remote Login state without root privileges. When run as a standard user, systemsetup -getremotelogin prints an administrator-access error and exits with status 0 instead of returning Off. Because the script only tries to enable SSH if the output matches Off, it skips the enablement step entirely. On a Mac that doesn’t already have SSH running, that mistake breaks the inbound access path, even though the SSH keys and persistence still get dropped.

值得注意的是，Phorion 发现了恶意软件尝试开启 SSH 时可能存在的疏漏。设置逻辑假设可以检查当前的远程登录状态，而无需 root 权限。当以普通用户运行时，systemsetup -getremotelogin 会打印管理员访问错误并以状态 0 退出，而不是返回 Off。因为脚本只有在输出匹配 Off 时才会尝试启用 SSH，因此完全跳过了启用步骤。在没有 SSH 正在运行的 Mac 上，这一错误会破坏入站访问路径，尽管 SSH 密钥和持久性仍然会被删除。

In this post, we’ll walk through how the backdoor works, why that macOS check fails, and what to look for across your fleet. The goal of this payload is long-term interactive access, and whilst the SSH backdoor bug minimises impact on macOS, the malware is still a significant threat that installs persistence and beacons host reconnaissance back to the operator.

在本文中，我们将逐步介绍 backdoor 的工作原理，分析该 macOS 检查为何失效，并说明在整个机群中需要关注什么。该 payload 的目标是长期交互式访问，尽管 SSH backdoor 漏洞最大限度地减少了对 macOS 的影响，但 malware 仍然是一个重大威胁，它会安装 persistence，并将主机侦察信息信标回传给 operator。

Infection Chain

感染链

The Cursor Marketplace Extension

Cursor 市场扩展

Cursor 市场扩展

介绍

Cursor 市场扩展允许你从 Cursor 市场浏览、安装和管理扩展。你可以发现适用于各种工作流程的扩展，从代码解释器到自定义语言支持。

浏览扩展

  1. 打开 Cursor 市场扩展面板：

    • 在 扩展 视图中点击 市场 标签
    • 或使用命令面板运行 Cursor: 浏览扩展

  2. 浏览分类：

    • 推荐 - 热门和精选扩展
    • 语言 - 语法高亮和语言支持
    • 编程语言 - 特定编程语言的支持
    • 调试 - 调试器和调试相关工具
    • 主题 - 外观主题和图标主题
    • 其他 - 其他类别

  3. 搜索扩展：

    • 使用搜索框按名称、描述或标签查找扩展

安装扩展

  1. 在扩展详情页点击 安装 按钮
  2. 安装完成后，扩展会自动激活
  3. 某些扩展可能需要重启编辑器才能生效

管理扩展

在 已安装 视图中你可以：

  • 启用/禁用 扩展
  • 卸载 不再需要的扩展
  • 更新 过期的扩展
  • 配置 扩展设置

发布你的扩展

如果你开发了一个扩展并希望分享到 Cursor 市场：

  1. 访问 Cursor 市场发布页面
  2. 打包你的扩展
  3. 登录你的 Cursor 账号
  4. 上传并发布

故障排除

如果遇到问题：

  • 确保你的 Cursor 已更新到最新版本
  • 检查扩展的兼容性要求
  • 查看扩展的 问题 选项卡报告 bug
  • 卸载并重新安装扩展

延伸阅读

  • Cursor 官方文档
  • 扩展开发指南
  • 市场服务条款

The compromised extension.js file starts with an injected immediately invoked function expression (IIFE) prepended to the minified extension bundle. The rest of the bundle looks like the standard extension, with Claude Code and VS Code strings, normal activate and deactivate exports, and UI code.

被攻击的 extension.js 文件以注入的立即调用函数表达式 (IIFE) 开头，该表达式前置于压缩的扩展包。其余部分看起来与标准扩展一致，包含 Claude Code 和 VS Code 字符串、正常的 activate 和 deactivate 导出以及 UI 代码。

The injected prefix pulls in standard Node.js modules (child_process, fs, os, path, http, and crypto) and executes as soon as Node loads the file, before the extension’s normal activate callback even runs. The user doesn’t need to interact with the extension for the payload to fire.

Because the malware appends to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys directly using Node’s fs.appendFileSync, process-only rules watching for shell commands like echo or tee touching authorized_keys won’t catch it. Even though the IDE binary itself is validly signed, its extension host process has no business modifying SSH authentication files in the background.

SSH Tunnels and Follow-On Access

SSH 隧道与后续访问

SSH 隧道是一种强大的网络技术，用于通过不安全网络（如互联网）安全地传输数据。它主要通过加密通道将流量从一个网络端口传输到另一个网络端口。

SSH 隧道类型

SSH 隧道主要分为两种类型：

本地端口转发（Local Port Forwarding）

本地端口转发允许你将本地机器的一个端口与远程服务器上的另一个端口建立连接。当你连接到本地端口时，数据会被加密并发送到远程服务器，然后被转发到指定的目标地址。

远程端口转发（Remote Port Forwarding）

远程端口转发的工作方式相反，允许你将远程服务器的一个端口与本地机器上的另一个端口建立连接。这对于在防火墙前面运行的服务非常有用。

设置 SSH 隧道

基本命令

ssh -L [本地端口]:[目标地址]:[目标端口] [用户名]@[SSH服务器]

例如，将本地端口 8080 转发到远程服务器上的本地服务：

ssh -L 8080:localhost:3000 user@remote-server.com

远程端口转发示例

ssh -R [远程端口]:[目标地址]:[目标端口] [用户名]@[SSH服务器]

例如，将远程服务器上的端口 9000 转发到本地机器上的数据库服务：

ssh -R 9000:localhost:5432 user@remote-server.com

持续运行 SSH 隧道

使用 -N 参数

当你只是想保持隧道持续运行而不需要执行远程命令时，使用 -N 参数可以防止 SSH 登录后执行默认命令：

ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:3000 user@remote-server.com

使用autossh

autossh 是一个基于 SSH 的工具，会自动监控连接并在连接断开时重新建立。这是在生产环境中维持 SSH 隧道持续运行的可靠方法：

autossh -M 0 -N -L 8080:localhost:3000 user@remote-server.com

其中 -M 0 表示禁用autossh的端口监控功能。

使用 tmux 或 screen

你可以将 SSH 命令放在 tmux 或 screen 会话中，以便在断开连接后继续运行：

tmux new-session -d -s tunnel 'ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:3000 user@remote-server.com'

SSH 隧道的后续访问

一旦 SSH 隧道建立，你可以像对待本地服务一样访问远程服务。这对于访问被防火墙保护的服务或通过不安全网络访问本地开发环境非常有用。

例如，如果你设置了一个本地端口转发将本地端口 8080 转发到远程服务器上的本地服务，你可以：

curl http://localhost:8080

这会通过加密的 SSH 隧道访问远程服务器上的本地服务。

性能考虑

SSH 隧道带有一定的开销，主要来自加密和解密操作。对于高性能需求的应用程序，可能会遇到性能瓶颈。

优化建议

  1. 使用较新的加密算法（如 Ed25519）
  2. 考虑在内部网络上使用更高效的隧道方案
  3. 对于临时访问，考虑使用 VPN 而不是持久 SSH 隧道

安全注意事项

  1. 始终使用强密码或 SSH 密钥进行身份验证
  2. 限制 SSH 隧道的用户权限
  3. 使用防火墙规则控制可访问的端口
  4. 定期更新和修补 SSH 软件

On the process and network side, look for:

在进程和网络方面，请关注：

  • ssh or autossh launched with remote port forwarding (-R *:0:localhost:22) and identity files pulled from /tmp/.stk_* or ~/.config/.smtk.
  • Outbound SSH connections to 134.209.82[.]225 on port 22, alongside HTTP POST requests to 134.209.82[.]225:8099 (and connection attempts to 127.0.0.1:8099).
  • 启动 ssh 或 autossh 并配合远程端口转发（-R *:0:localhost:22），身份文件从 /tmp/.stk_* 或 ~/.config/.smtk 中获取。
  • 向 134.209.82[.]225 的 22 端口发起出站 SSH 连接，同时向 134.209.82[.]225:8099 发送 HTTP POST 请求（并尝试连接 127.0.0.1:8099）。

If you find a host where this extension ran, it’s important to check whether the tunnel was merely established or whether an operator actually logged in through it. Because inbound sessions arrive through the local port forward, successful logins in SSH logs will appear to come from localhost (127.0.0.1 or ::1) authenticating with the svc-telemetry key.

如果您发现了运行此扩展程序的主机，关键在于确认该隧道是仅处于连接建立状态，还是确实有操作员通过它进行了登录。由于传入会话是通过本地端口转发到达的，SSH 日志中的成功登录记录将显示为来自 localhost（127.0.0.1 或 ::1），并使用 svc-telemetry 密钥进行身份验证。

Remediation

整改

  1. Kill active tunnel processes: Terminate the /bin/sh retry loop and any ssh or autossh processes connecting to 134.209.82[.]225.
  2. Remove persistence: Unload and delete ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.sysmond.plist on macOS (or clean up the @reboot cron entry on Linux / SysMon scheduled task and Startup script on Windows), and remove ~/.config/.smt and ~/.config/.smtk.

  4. Rotate credentials: If SSH was enabled on the host, or if there’s any evidence of an inbound login, rotate any credentials or tokens that were accessible to that user account (especially those matching the KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|AWS|GCP environment variable filter).
  1. 终止活动隧道进程： 终止 /bin/sh 重试循环和任何连接到 134.209.82[.]225 的 ssh 或 autossh 进程。

  4. 旋转凭据： 如果 SSH 在主机上启用，或者存在入站登录的任何证据，则旋转该用户账户可访问的所有凭据或令牌（尤其是匹配 KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|AWS|GCP 环境变量过滤的）。
